title: AlphaTensor finds faster ways to multiply small binary matrices, and independent mathematicians build on them
summary: DeepMind's AlphaTensor found ways to multiply 4x4 matrices over the field with two elements in 47 multiplications and 5x5 matrices in 96; two mathematicians then cut the 5x5 count to 95.
account: On 5 October 2022, Nature published AlphaTensor, a reinforcement-learning system from DeepMind (Fawzi, Balog, Huang, Hubert, Romera-Paredes and others). The system treats the search for matrix multiplication algorithms as a one-player game called TensorGame. A deep neural network guides a planning procedure derived from AlphaZero. AlphaTensor found an algorithm multiplying two 4x4 matrices over the field with two elements in 47 multiplications. That beat Strassen's two-level algorithm, which needs 49, for the first time in about 50 years. AlphaTensor also found a 96-multiplication scheme for 5x5 matrices over that field. On 8 October 2022, Manuel Kauers and Jakob Moosbauer of Johannes Kepler University Linz posted a preprint, which they revised on 13 October. They started from the published 5x5 scheme and improved it to 95 multiplications. On 2 December 2022 they posted a further preprint. Its peer-reviewed version appeared on 24 July 2023 in the proceedings of the International Symposium on Symbolic and Algebraic Computation. With a search method that uses no learning, they found more than 100,000 further 4x4 schemes with 47 multiplications over the field with two elements. None of these schemes could be lifted to the integers modulo 4. Their search reached 95 multiplications for 5x5 matrices only when it started from AlphaTensor's scheme. From the standard algorithm it reached 97. In February 2025, Moosbauer and Poole reported 93 multiplications for 5x5 matrices over any field, below AlphaTensor's 96.
purpose: Built to discover matrix multiplication algorithms by searching for low-rank tensor decompositions; the new schemes were that purpose.
system: AlphaTensor (AlphaZero-derived reinforcement learning for tensor decomposition)

ratings.reason: Researchers in algebraic complexity gained new explicit decompositions, and Kauers and Moosbauer improved the 5x5 one within a week. The gains hold only over particular fields. Nature reports the 4x4 improvement for matrices “in a finite field”, and Kauers and Moosbauer give the 5x5 record of 96 multiplications over the field with two elements.

ai_role.statement: The reinforcement-learning agent found the 47-multiplication 4x4 scheme and the 96-multiplication 5x5 scheme. Kauers and Moosbauer report that their flip-graph search, which uses no learning, reached only 97 for 5x5 from the standard algorithm and reached 95 when it started from AlphaTensor's scheme. The same search found a 4x4 by 4x5 scheme of rank 60 from the standard algorithm, valid modulo 2, where AlphaTensor had found 63.

display.answer: The DeepMind authors' paper in Nature is the primary source. Kauers and Moosbauer, who work at Johannes Kepler University Linz and have no tie to DeepMind, wrote the preprint and the peer-reviewed paper, and both build on the published AlphaTensor schemes.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: DeepMind's AlphaTensor found ways to multiply 4x4 matrices over the field with two elements in 47 multiplications and 5x5 matrices in 96; two mathematicians then cut the 5x5 count to 95.
fields.account: On 5 October 2022, Nature published AlphaTensor, a reinforcement-learning system from DeepMind (Fawzi, Balog, Huang, Hubert, Romera-Paredes and others). The system treats the search for matrix multiplication algorithms as a one-player game called TensorGame. A deep neural network guides a planning procedure derived from AlphaZero. AlphaTensor found an algorithm multiplying two 4x4 matrices over the field with two elements in 47 multiplications. That beat Strassen's two-level algorithm, which needs 49, for the first time in about 50 years. AlphaTensor also found a 96-multiplication scheme for 5x5 matrices over that field. On 8 October 2022, Manuel Kauers and Jakob Moosbauer of Johannes Kepler University Linz posted a preprint, which they revised on 13 October. They started from the published 5x5 scheme and improved it to 95 multiplications. On 2 December 2022 they posted a further preprint. Its peer-reviewed version appeared on 24 July 2023 in the proceedings of the International Symposium on Symbolic and Algebraic Computation. With a search method that uses no learning, they found more than 100,000 further 4x4 schemes with 47 multiplications over the field with two elements. None of these schemes could be lifted to the integers modulo 4. Their search reached 95 multiplications for 5x5 matrices only when it started from AlphaTensor's scheme. From the standard algorithm it reached 97. In February 2025, Moosbauer and Poole reported 93 multiplications for 5x5 matrices over any field, below AlphaTensor's 96.
